a: A hidden-role mafia party game for a room of friends, the game Greeks know as Palermo, a cousin of Mafia and Werewolf. Your phone holds your secret card, the TV shows the town, and a noir narrator runs every night, so nobody has to sit out to lead the game.

q: How many players do we need?
a: From 6 to 14. By default the town hides two killers up to 11 players, and three from 12. The host picks the roles and the timers before the deal, or starts from a preset: Classic, Quick or Full house.

q: What do we need to play?
a: A phone each and one screen the whole room can see: a smart TV's browser, or a laptop on the TV. Open vgraphics.gr/tv on the screen and type the room code; friends scan the QR code to join. Nothing to install.
Yes, with every role in. Ads only show outside play, between games and never during one.
No. Join as a guest, or with your free VHub name, which keeps your games, XP and achievements across every VGraphics game. The TV signs in as a screen, never as a person.
It's for ages 13 and up. Each phone gives its year of birth once and only an age group is kept, never the year.
English or Greek. The narrator, the cards and every screen follow the host's language.
Rooms for your group open soon: on the web first, then on Android. Until then, the guided demo seats you at a table of bots in your browser, today. Every release shows under What's new on this page.

A room closes 30 minutes after its last phone goes offline, or 8 hours after it opened, and is deleted 24 hours after it closes. A short summary of each game, with no names, identifiers or votes, is kept for 12 months. Analytics runs only with your consent. The privacy policy has the details.

q: Where can I read the rules?
a: In the wiki: every role, every card in the Lawyer's briefcase, and how a round plays, from the deal to the verdict.
